title: portable linux: keep the original Rscript binary
description:
Unfortunately Rscript behaves differently from the current replacement shell script, e.g. the shell script starts an interactive R shell if I call it without arguments, instead of printing the help like the original Rscript binary does. 

I am sure that there are other differences as well, and the differences might change over R versions, so in general we probably don't want to track these differences.

Why not simplify the shell script to simply setting `RHOME` and calling the original Rscript binary? That should work for all R versions we care about.

Something like this should do, this is what I use on macOS:
```
#!/bin/sh
RHOME=$(cd "$(dirname "$(realpath "$0")")/.." && pwd -P)
export RHOME
exec "$(dirname "$(realpath "$0")")/Rscript.orig" "$@"
```

Is there anything against this?

title: Portable `Rscript` doesn't handle trailing args after `-e`
description:
## Description

In the `portable-r` build, the compiled `Rscript` binary is replaced with a "relocatable wrapper". This wrapper aims to mimic the behaviour of `Rscript`.

If the wrapper is invoked with one or more `-e` arguments (i.e. expressions to evaluate), any trailing positional arguments are discarded.


## Example

```console
user@host:~$ Rscript -e 'print(commandArgs(trailing = TRUE))'
character(0)
user@host:~$
user@host:~$ Rscript -e 'print(commandArgs(trailing = TRUE))' ARG1=one ARG2=two
ARGUMENT 'ARG1=one' __ignored__

ARGUMENT 'ARG2=two' __ignored__

character(0)
user@host:~$
```

## Cause

The current implementation assumes that once `-e` has been seen, the remaining arguments can be passed directly to R:

https://github.com/rstudio/r-builds/blob/8139849bb24e2ad94738cbfdd9ee21379a18a7cd/builder/portable-r/make-relocatable.sh#L101-L102

https://github.com/rstudio/r-builds/blob/8139849bb24e2ad94738cbfdd9ee21379a18a7cd/builder/portable-r/make-relocatable.sh#L122-L123

However, `R` and `Rscript` differ with respect to how trailing args should be passed:

* `R` expects trailing args to follow a `--args` flag - more details here: https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/doc/manual/R-intro.html#Invoking-R-from-the-command-line-1
* `Rscript` expects trailing args to simply follow the provided filepath or `-e` argument - docs here: https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/doc/manual/R-intro.html#Invoking-R-from-the-command-line-1

So when at least one `-e` argument is present, the wrapper currently constructs a command that looks like `R -e "..." [args]`, rather than `R -e "..." --args [args]`. This leads to the `ARGUMENT  __ignored__` error seen above.


## Possible solution

Rather than passing args through to R as soon as we encounter an `-e` argument, I think we'll need to "collect" these arguments in a similar way to how we already collect `--options`, and then ultimately to construct an R command using everything we have collected... I'll open a PR attempting this!


## Example of a downstream consequence

Like #309, I first came across this when trying to run `future::plan(future::multisession)`. After applying the patch for #309, I was still unable to successfully run that expression - I instead saw lots of errors like the following:

```
`ARGUMENT 'MASTER=localhost' __ignored__
ARGUMENT 'PORT=11540' __ignored__
[...]

Error in workRSOCK() : PORT must be specified
Execution halted
[...]
```

Again this is from deep in the internals of {parallelly}, where [its attempt to launch a parallel worker](https://github.com/futureverse/parallelly/blob/6b38896d1b1441e66752b52aa2ab73dcbbc9243e/R/makeNodePSOCK.R#L878) using {parallel} fails because [the expected command args](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/cf5d0a0bb283f54d1c69438efe2c47dda0846da1/src/library/parallel/R/snowSOCK.R#L384) aren't found.

title: Portable `Rscript --version` returns nothing
description:
## Description

In the `portable-r` build, the compiled `Rscript` binary is replaced with a "relocatable wrapper". This wrapper aims to mimic the behaviour of `Rscript`.

When the wrapper is invoked with the `--version` flag, at present, nothing is returned:

```console
user@host:~$ Rscript --version
user@host:~$
```


## Cause

The implementation of `--version` uses R to compose a version string, in particular depending on information the `R.version` object:

https://github.com/rstudio/r-builds/blob/944cf9ec4215f03289d81dbbc09d07d37f95b998/builder/portable-r/make-relocatable.sh#L92-L93

However, it looks like `R.version$date` doesn't exist at all, since at least R 4.5.2:

<details><summary>R 4.5.2 for Windows (r-project.org)</summary>

```
> R.version
               _
platform       x86_64-w64-mingw32
arch           x86_64
os             mingw32
crt            ucrt
system         x86_64, mingw32
status
major          4
minor          5.2
year           2025
month          10
day            31
svn rev        88974
language       R
version.string R version 4.5.2 (2025-10-31 ucrt)
nickname       [Not] Part in a Rumble
```

</details>

<details><summary>R 4.6.0 for manylinux (rstudio/r-builds)</summary>

```
> R.version
               _                           
platform       aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu   
arch           aarch64                     
os             linux-gnu                   
system         aarch64, linux-gnu          
status                                     
major          4                           
minor          6.0                         
year           2026                        
month          04                          
day            24                          
svn rev        89956                       
language       R                           
version.string R version 4.6.0 (2026-04-24)
nickname       Because it was There 
```

</details>

Instead we have individual date components in `R.version$year` etc.

(I'm not sure whether this changed recently - I did have a look in the R changelog, but couldn't find any mention of `R.version$date`.)

Consequently, one of the arguments passed to `sprintf()` is `NULL`, meaning we end up with `cat(character(0))` and therefore no output.


## Possible solution

We can use other elements of `R.version` to compose the date manually - I'll put in a PR with that fix!


## Example of a downstream consequence

I came across this while trying to run `future::plan(future::multisession)` - it failed with the following opaque error message:

```r
future::plan(future::multisession)
#> Error in if (!grepl(getRversion(), out, fixed = TRUE)) { : 
#>  argument is of length zero
```

After chasing through several layers, it turns out that the {parallelly} package tries to assert that `Rscript` is available on the system by [checking that `Rscript --version` returns an acceptable response](https://github.com/futureverse/parallelly/blob/47d93f8f2675287ec7da40fdea9bf043efea488f/R/utils.R#L158).

title: Error loading packages in Fedora 42 build
description:
I've been running into trouble installing R via [`rig`](https://github.com/r-lib/rig) on Fedora 42 (6.14.9-300.fc42.x86_64) and I think I've chased the issue down to coming from the `r-builds` binary that rig is installing; i.e. I installed directly from `r-builds` instead of via `rig` and the issue is still happening.

R installs fine, but when running R, either interactively or otherwise, it immediately warns:

```
> During startup - Warning messages:
> 1: package ‘utils’ in options("defaultPackages") was not found 
> 2: package ‘stats’ in options("defaultPackages") was not found 
```

After that, in the REPL, R will error on anything trying to call anything from outside of `base`, saying "could not find function". A quick check confirms that the packages are in the location given by `.Library`, as expected, so the problem isn't that they're not getting installed. 

If you attempt to load a library e.g. `library("utils")`, you get:

```
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘utils’:
 .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'utils', details:
  call: system(paste(which, shQuote(names[i])), intern = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE)
  error: error in running command
```

If [this post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60037359/onload-failed-in-loadnamespace-for-utils-details) is an indication, this seems like it could be a problem with the system call R is making to `which` - perhaps the system install location of `which` on Fedora 42 is different from where R expected it to be when built? At least, I haven't done anything to change the install location of `which`, so I assume this is a change related to the Fedora 42 release. From scanning the Fedora 42 changelog for relevant changes, perhaps it's related to [Fedora 42's unifying of `/usr/bin` and `/usr/sbin`](https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Releases/42/ChangeSet#Unify_/usr/bin_and_/usr/sbin)?

Oracle Linux 9 support
description:

title: HTTPUserAgent is set to empty character vector on Debian testing/unstable
description:
I am using some of the deb packages built through this repo on Debian unstable. I believe that this is not an officially supported OS, so you might not want to act on this, however the fix looks to be straightforward.

The underlying issue is related to `/etc/os-release`: in Debian unstable and testing, the `VERSION` and `VERSION_ID` variables (which [are optional](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/os-release.html#VERSION_ID=)) are removed until close to the next release date.

The result when using the R package on such a system is:

```R
> getOption("HTTPUserAgent")
character(0)
```

which violates expectations of downstream packages such as `renv` which assume that `HTTPUserAgent` is either `NULL` or a nonempty character vector. (`renv` is rendered completely unable to install packages, which is how I noticed this issue.)

This is related to the following lines inserted by the build script into Rprofile (as of #34):

https://github.com/rstudio/r-builds/blob/5532edb31d5f9cd3689b7bf61dc02d17d1b6dbde/builder/build.sh#L183-L195

When the `VERSION_ID` is missing from `/etc/os-release`, `grep("^VERSION_ID=", os, value = TRUE)` returns `character(0)`, which then "infects" the rest of this section including `HTTPUserAgent`:

```R
> os <- readLines("/etc/os-release")
> os
[1] "PRETTY_NAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux trixie/sid\""   
[2] "NAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux\""                     
[3] "VERSION_CODENAME=trixie"                       
[4] "ID=debian"                                     
[5] "HOME_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/\""          
[6] "SUPPORT_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/support\""
[7] "BUG_REPORT_URL=\"https://bugs.debian.org/\""   
> id <- gsub('^ID=|"', "", grep("^ID=", os, value = TRUE))
> id
[1] "debian"
> version <- gsub('^VERSION_ID=|"', "", grep("^VERSION_ID=", os, value = TRUE))
> version
character(0)
> sprintf("%s-%s", id, version) 
character(0)
```

Proposed fix: in the above lines, if `version` is equal to `character(0)`, either set it to some dummy value (e.g. `"0"`), or make sure that `HTTPUserAgent` is set to `NULL` in this case.

title: RHEL 8 and 9 R binaries no longer compatible with EPEL 8 and 9
description:
It looks like Fedora/EPEL R has switched to linking against [FlexiBLAS](https://www.mpi-magdeburg.mpg.de/projects/flexiblas), a new library for runtime switching of BLAS/LAPACK that defaults to OpenBLAS:

https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Changes/FlexiBLAS_as_BLAS/LAPACK_manager
https://developer.fedoraproject.org/tech/languages/r/blas-lapack.html

The R package from EPEL 9 is now built against FlexiBLAS, and the R from EPEL 8 is now built against the OpenMP version of OpenBLAS (perhaps because FlexiBLAS isn't available?). EPEL 7 R is still built against the shared BLAS.

Unfortunately, these changes mean the RHEL 8 and 9 R binaries are no longer compatible with EPEL R, which mostly affects Package Manager's binary packages, as BLAS-using packages don't work out of box with EPEL R anymore:
```r
# RHEL 9
install.packages("Matrix", repos = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/rhel9/latest")
library(Matrix)
# Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘Matrix’ in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...):
#  unable to load shared object '/usr/lib64/R/library/Matrix/libs/Matrix.so':
#   libRlapack.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

For RHEL 9, it seems like a good idea to switch to FlexiBLAS (probably starting from R 4.3), and the R admin docs have it documented as well: https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-devel/R-admin.html#BLAS

For RHEL 8, I'm not sure what to do as EPEL R is now hard linked to openblas-openmp. We might just leave that as-is and accept the incompatibility. A workaround to use Package Manager binary packages could be to symlink OpenBLAS to R's shared BLAS/LAPACK locations:
```sh
ln -s /usr/lib64/libopenblaso.so $(R RHOME)/lib/libRblas.so
ln -s /usr/lib64/libopenblaso.so $(R RHOME)/lib/libRlapack.so
```

title: Broken R installation on openSUSE 15.3 because of ICU 69 update
description:
SUSE has released a security update to add ICU 69 to openSUSE 15.3 and SLES 15 SP3, which is a major version upgrade from the original ICU 65 (https://lists.suse.com/pipermail/sle-security-updates/2021-December/009908.html).

While the libraries for ICU 65 and 69 can be installed together, the devel packages can't, and zypper now resolves `libicu-devel` (ICU 65) to the new `icu.691-devel` (ICU 69) package. The R binaries currently use ICU 65, so they now install a broken R:
```sh
$ curl -O https://cdn.rstudio.com/r/opensuse-153/pkgs/R-4.1.2-1-1.x86_64.rpm

$ zypper install R-4.1.2-1-1.x86_64.rpm 

$ /opt/R/4.1.2/bin/R
/opt/R/4.1.2/lib/R/bin/exec/R: error while loading shared libraries: libicuuc.so.suse65.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

We'll probably change the openSUSE 15.3 builds to use ICU 69 instead. It's now the default, and there doesn't seem to be a way to get the devel package for ICU 65 installed anyway.

title: jq missing as bionic dependency (compared to r-core)
description:
Dockerfile showing the lack of `jq` when using the r-builds bionic installer.

```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:bionic-20190912.1

RUN export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    curl && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install R and make it default.
ARG R_VERSION=3.4.4
ARG OS_IDENTIFIER=ubuntu-1804
RUN curl -L -O https://cdn.rstudio.com/r/${OS_IDENTIFIER}/pkgs/r-${R_VERSION}_1_amd64.deb && \
    export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -f -y ./r-${R_VERSION}_1_amd64.deb && \
    ln -s /opt/R/${R_VERSION}/bin/R /usr/bin/R && \
    ln -s /opt/R/${R_VERSION}/bin/Rscript /usr/bin/Rscript && \
    ln -s /opt/R/${R_VERSION}/lib/R /usr/lib/R && \
    rm r-${R_VERSION}_1_amd64.deb && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN jq --help
```

When building this `Dockerfile`, we get the error:
```
Step 6/6 : RUN jq --help
 ---> Running in c70358551411
/bin/sh: 1: jq: not found
The command '/bin/sh -c jq --help' returned a non-zero code: 127
```

Compare this against the result of installing `r-base` from the Ubuntu repository.

```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:bionic-20190912.1

RUN export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    curl && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    r-base && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN jq --help
```

This `Dockerfile` successfully builds. The `jq` utility is installed as a consequence of installing `r-base`.

Workaround:

Explicitly install `jq`.

```dockerfile
# Install jq as a standalone step. Also fine as an addition to the earlier apt-get install.
RUN export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    jq
```

title: Default pager is specific to Ubuntu/Debian
description:
On CentOS and openSUSE, help pages and `file.show()` fail because `/usr/bin/pager` doesn't exist:
```sh
# R 3.5.3 on CentOS 7

> ?print
/opt/R/3.5.3/lib/R/bin/pager: line 11: /usr/bin/pager: No such file or directory
Warning message:
error in running command 

> file.show("test.txt")
/opt/R/3.5.3/lib/R/bin/pager: line 11: /usr/bin/pager: No such file or directory
Warning message:
error in running command
```

I think it's because the default pager is configured as `/usr/bin/pager`, which seems to be an Ubuntu/Debian specific thing. https://unix.stackexchange.com/questions/5383/which-systems-have-pager-shortcut-alias/5404#5404
https://github.com/rstudio/r-builds/blob/b822b418a0b9d7db9b2ba418d3bc3bf35107463f/builder/build.sh#L76

---

From the R docs, if `PAGER` isn't set, R defaults to `less` if available and `more` as a fallback:
> The ‘factory-fresh’ default is to use ‘R_HOME/bin/pager’, which is a shell script running the command-line specified by the environment variable PAGER whose default is set at configuration, usually to less. On a Unix-alike more is used if pager is empty.
> https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/options.html

So I think we could fix this by setting `PAGER=/usr/bin/pager` for Ubuntu and Debian builds only, and letting CentOS/openSUSE builds use the default. It should be `more` on the openSUSE images and `less` on CentOS images (but we may want to remove `less` as a dependency).

title: manylinux 2.28 build segfaults on `x11()` on Ubuntu 26.04
description:
The manylinux build bundles the X stack into lib/R/lib/.libs. But bundled libX11 was built with `USE_DYNAMIC_XCURSOR`, so at cursor creation it does `dlopen("libXcursor.so.1")`. This is a hard-coded, unmangled string, but there is no libXcursor in the bundle.

So this brings in system libXrender + libX11, which crashes. (Trace below.)

A workaround is to give the dlopen a harmless target that wins via bundled libX11':

```
ln -s libXau-54347979.so.6 <R>/lib/R/lib/.libs/libXcursor.so.1
```

A proper fix is to configure libX11 with `--disable-loadable-xcursor`, or to bundle a real `libXcursor.so.1`.
